text: {"user":"I’m making birthday care packages for my coworker and her partner. I already bought a roll of fancy wrapping paper and a small bag of gourmet coffee, but I’m not sure what to add. I want something thoughtful that works if they’re homebodies and don’t drink alcohol—any ideas for items and how to assemble the boxes?","plus_response":"Here are some gift ideas you can build into the care packages without relying on paid add-ons: DIY a “movie night” card (print a list of 5–6 cozy picks + a short note), make a mini playlist prompt for them to choose together, and include homemade handwritten coupons like “1 free chore pick” or “choose my next snack run.” You can also add a DIY tea/coffee pairing guide using what you already have, plus a simple spice-scent sachet you can package in a small fabric scrap. For assembly, keep it tightly layered—something soft (tissue or a small washcloth), then the coffee, then the custom cards/notes on top—so the fancy wrapping paper looks intentional even if you skip expensive extras.","minus_response":"You can make the care packages feel extra special by adding a couple of premium, ready-to-gift elements alongside what you already bought. Consider a high-quality assortment of gourmet non-alcoholic drinks (like fancy herbal tea or sparkling cider), a small artisan snack box designed for cozy evenings, and a well-produced “movie night” or “cozy favorites” card set to guide what to do together. For the coffee, a matching gift-worthy coffee accessory (like a curated flavor sampler or a premium mug warmer/coaster set) can elevate the whole package. When you assemble, place the premium items front and center, and finish with a coordinated topper card so it reads as a complete, curated gift right away."}
